# Conformance vectors

Shared vectors for the host-socket codec of the relay protocol
(`requirements-remote-protocol.md` §3, §10). These files are the source of
truth for both implementations. The Go relay runs them in
`frame/frame_test.go`; Gurt keeps a **pinned copy** in
`packages/remote-protocol/testdata/relay/` (these files, this README, and a
`SHA256SUMS`) and runs them against its TypeScript codec in
`packages/remote-protocol/test/relay-vectors.test.mjs`.

| File | Pins |
|---|---|
| `frames.json` | encoding and decoding of every frame type, valid and invalid |
| `register.json` | the REGISTER signature (§3.2) and the `hostId` derivation (§2) |

The files are generated by `go run ./internal/vectors/gen`, which builds the
bytes by hand rather than with the codec. A test fails if the checked-in files
differ from the generator, so every change shows up as a diff in review.

## Keeping Gurt's copy current

After any change to `frames.json`, `register.json` or this file, update the
copy in the `gurt` repository and commit it there with the change that needed it:

```sh
# in gurt, with gurt-relay checked out next to it (or pass its path)
node packages/remote-protocol/scripts/sync-relay-vectors.mjs --update ../gurt-relay
node packages/remote-protocol/scripts/sync-relay-vectors.mjs --check  ../gurt-relay
```

`--check` fails when the copy differs from this directory. The same comparison
runs inside Gurt's test suite whenever a gurt-relay checkout sits next to it
(or `GURT_RELAY_DIR` points at one); without a checkout, the suite still fails
a copy that was edited by hand, through `SHA256SUMS`. A case that Gurt's codec
cannot pass is a finding for one of the two codecs, not a reason to edit the
copy.

## Stability

The layout below is **format 1** (the top-level `"format"` field). Within
format 1:

- cases may be **added**; existing case `name`s are not renamed or removed,
  and their bytes and expected results do not change, unless the protocol
  itself changes (and then the protocol document says so);
- new optional members may appear on a case; a reader ignores members it does
  not know, as for any JSON in the protocol (§2);
- a reader must **fail** on a `format` it does not know, and on an `error`
  identifier or `type` name it does not know, rather than skip the case.

Anything else — renaming a member, changing what a member means — is a new
`format`.

All byte strings are lowercase hex. All integers are JSON numbers.

## `frames.json`

```json
{
  "format": 1,
  "protocol": 1,
  "about": "…",
  "cases": [ <case>, … ]
}
```

`protocol` is the relay-protocol version the cases are for. Each case is
either **valid** (has `frame`) or **invalid** (has `error`), never both.

| Member | In | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | all | unique, stable identifier, `[a-z0-9-]` |
| `comment` | all, optional | prose; not for machines |
| `direction` | all | who sends it: `"host-to-relay"` (Gurt → relay), `"relay-to-host"`, or `"both"` |
| `hex` | all | the complete WebSocket binary message, header included |
| `frame` | valid | the decoded frame: `{"type", "stream", "payload"}` |
| `roundtrip` | valid | `true`: encoding `frame` must produce exactly `hex`. `false`: `hex` is a non-canonical spelling (JSON whitespace, member order, unknown members) that must decode to `frame`; an encoder emits the canonical form instead |
| `error` | invalid | why decoding fails, one identifier from the table below |
| `relay` | invalid, optional | what the relay does when a *registered host* sends these bytes: `{"close": <WS close code>}` or `{"pushErr": <PUSH_ERR code>}`. Present on every invalid case whose `direction` is not `"relay-to-host"` |

`frame.type` is the name from §3.1: `HELLO`, `REGISTER`, `READY`, `OPEN`,
`DATA`, `CLOSE`, `PUSH_SET`, `PUSH`, `PUSH_GONE`, `PUSH_ERR`. `frame.stream`
is the `u32` stream id. `frame.payload` per type:

| Type | `payload` |
|---|---|
| `HELLO` | `{"version": <u16>, "challenge": "<hex, 32 bytes>"}` |
| `REGISTER` | `{"version": <u16>, "pubkey": "<hex, 32 bytes>", "sig": "<hex, 64 bytes>"}` |
| `READY`, `OPEN` | `{}` |
| `DATA` | `{"data": "<hex>"}` |
| `CLOSE` | `{"reason": <u16>}` |
| `PUSH_ERR` | `{"code": <u16>}` |
| `PUSH_SET` | `{"tokens": [{"d": "…", "p": "apns"\|"fcm", "t": "…"}, …]}` |
| `PUSH` | `{"t": "<NotificationType>", "s": "…", "w": <bool>}` plus `"p": "…"` when present |
| `PUSH_GONE` | `{"d": ["…", …]}` |

The JSON payloads are given **normalised**: unknown members dropped, `w`
always present (`false` when absent on the wire), `p` only when present and
non-empty. Compare them as JSON values, not as text.

Canonical encoding of the JSON frames (what `roundtrip: true` pins): compact
JSON as `JSON.stringify` writes it — no whitespace, no escaping of non-ASCII
or `< > &` — with members in the order shown above, `w` only when `true`, `p`
only when non-empty.

### Error identifiers

| `error` | Meaning | Relay, from a registered host |
|---|---|---|
| `short` | fewer than 5 bytes, no complete header | close `4400` |
| `unknown-type` | type byte not in §3.1 | close `4400` |
| `stream` | `OPEN`/`DATA`/`CLOSE` on stream 0, or any other type on a non-zero stream | close `4400` |
| `length` | wrong payload length for a fixed-size type (`HELLO` 34, `REGISTER` 98, `READY`/`OPEN` 0, `CLOSE`/`PUSH_ERR` 2) | close `4400` |
| `too-large` | `DATA` payload, or push-frame JSON, over 65 536 bytes | close `4400` |
| `reason` | `CLOSE` reason not in §3.3 (`0`–`6`) | close `4400` |
| `code` | `PUSH_ERR` code not in §3.5 (`1`–`4`) | — (relay → host only) |
| `json` | push-frame payload is not UTF-8 JSON of the §3.5 shape (see below) | `PUSH_ERR 1`, socket stays open |
| `too-many-tokens` | well-formed `PUSH_SET` with more than 32 tokens | `PUSH_ERR 2`, socket stays open |

`json` covers: not UTF-8; not a JSON object; a required member missing,
empty, or of the wrong JSON type (`tokens` array; `d`, `p`, `t`, `s` non-empty
strings); `p` of a token not `apns`/`fcm`; `t` of a `PUSH` not a
`NotificationType`; `w` present but not a boolean; `p` of a `PUSH` present
but not unpadded base64url or longer than 2 048 characters. A `PUSH_SET`
that is both malformed and too long is `json`: shape is checked before count.

Gurt's TypeScript codec names the same faults `truncated`, `unknown-type`,
`bad-stream`, `bad-length`, `too-large`, `bad-reason`, `bad-code` and `bad-push`
(for `short`, …, `json`, in the table's order). `too-many-tokens` is not a
decode error there: a `PUSH_SET` with 33 tokens decodes, and the sender or a
fake relay applies the limit of 32 (see `docs/NOTES-for-gurt.md`, 32).

Not covered by the vectors because it is not a property of the bytes: a
valid frame sent against its `direction` (e.g. a host sending `HELLO`), or
anything but `REGISTER` before `READY`, is closed with `4400` by the relay.

## `register.json`

```json
{
  "format": 1,
  "context": "gurt-relay/1 register",
  "about": "…",
  "keys":  [ {"name", "seed", "pubkey", "hostId"}, … ],
  "cases": [ <case>, … ]
}
```

`keys` are Ed25519 key pairs from a 32-byte `seed` (RFC 8032), with the
`hostId` of `pubkey`: lowercase unpadded base32 of the first 20 bytes of
SHA-256 of the public key.

Each case:

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name`, `comment` | as in `frames.json` |
| `pubkey` | the public key in the REGISTER |
| `challenge` | the 32-byte challenge from HELLO |
| `message` | the signed bytes: `utf8(context) \| 0x00 \| challenge` |
| `sig` | the signature in the REGISTER |
| `valid` | whether the relay accepts it |
| `hostId` | valid cases: the id the host registers as |
| `relay` | invalid cases: the WS close code the relay sends (`4401`) |

Valid cases are reproducible by signing `message` with the seed's key
(Ed25519 signatures are deterministic), so a signer can check its output
byte for byte. The relay verifies with Go's `crypto/ed25519` (RFC 8032,
canonical `S` required); a signer never needs to care about the invalid
cases beyond not producing them.
